explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose
   - This is Weasis, an open-source, modular, desktop and web-capable DICOM viewer platform written in Java. It uses a plugin/OSGi-style architecture to load and run a family of image viewers (2D, 3D, SR, ECG, RT, audio, etc.), acquisition tools, and distribution scripts, all orchestrated via a Launcher module.

2. Analyze the file structure
   - Top-level pom.xml defines a multi-module Maven build.
   - Key modules:
     • weasis-launcher: the Java Swing entry point and OSGi bootstrapping container.
     • weasis-core: core APIs (image I/O, plugin registry, task management, GUI abstractions).
     • weasis-base: foundational “base” UI and explorer libraries.
     • weasis-dicom: a parent with submodules for DICOM viewers (viewer2d, viewer3d), explorers, codecs, services (AU, SR, RT, wave).
     • weasis-acquire: image acquisition editor and explorer.
     • weasis-imageio: image-codec utilities independent from DICOM.
     • weasis-distributions & snap: packaging (installers, Docker, Snapcraft).
     • tests & archetype: integration tests and a project archetype for custom plugins.
   - Configuration files: OSGi activators, META-INF, layout XMLs, Maven build workflows, Dockerfile, snapcraft.yaml.

3. Examine the README for additional insights
   - Confirms a plugin API for custom viewers.
   - Lists DICOM network features (C-GET, C-MOVE, WADO, STOW-RS), DICOM export (ISO, ZIP, DICOMDIR).
   - Mentions desktop and web launch modes, high-DPI Swing UI, multi-language support.

4. How to draw the system design diagram
   a. Main components (draw each as a colored box or swimlane):
      1. Launcher Layer
         • weasis-launcher (AppLauncher, OSGi container)
      2. Core Layer
         • weasis-core (API, plugin registry, task monitor, GUI abstractions)
         • weasis-base (UI widgets, explorer framework)
      3. Plugin Modules
         • weasis-dicom modules (viewer2d, viewer3d, explorer, codec, SR, AU, RT, wave)
         • weasis-acquire (editor + explorer)
         • weasis-imageio (media codecs)
      4. Packaging Layer
         • weasis-distributions / snap / Docker / installers
      5. External Services
         • PACS/DICOMWeb server (Query/Retrieve, StoreSCU, STOW-RS)
   b. Relationships and interactions (draw arrows):
      • weasis-launcher → loads → weasis-core & weasis-base bundles via OSGi
      • Plugins register with → core plugin registry
      • UI modules invoke → core API for image loading, processing, network calls
      • DICOM modules communicate over TCP/HTTP → external PACS/DICOMWeb
      • Packaging scripts consume → Maven artifacts to produce installers
   c. Architectural patterns and principles
      • Plugin/OSGi modularity: dynamic bundle loading
      • MVC/MVP-style separation: core API vs. viewer components vs. UI
      • Layered architecture: Launcher → Core → Plugins → External
      • Inversion of Control: modules register via Activator
   d. Technologies & frameworks
      • Java 8+ / Swing
      • Maven multi-module build
      • OSGi bundle lifecycle (Activator classes)
      • Snapcraft, Docker, native installers
      • DICOM networking (dcm4che or custom)
      • JSON/XML configs for layouts and preferences

5. Guidelines for tailoring the diagram
   - Emphasize separation:
     • top row: Launcher & OSGi container
     • middle row: Core API & Base UI
     • next row: Functional plugins (group by DICOM viewers, acquisition, codecs)
     • bottom row: Packaging and external services
   - Show plugin extension points (e.g., DataExplorerViewFactory, ViewerFactory)
   - For DICOM network, show modules making C-GET/C-MOVE/WADO arrows to PACS
   - For 3D viewer, show jogamp/OpenGL dependency

6. Elements to include in the diagram
   - Clear labels on each module box (use module artifact-id)
   - Directional arrows for “loads,” “registers,” “calls,” “communicates”
   - Color coding:
     • Launcher (blue)
     • Core/Base (green)
     • Plugins (orange grouped by functionality)
     • Packaging (gray)
     • External services (purple)
   - Shapes:
     • Rectangles for modules
     • Cylinders for external servers/databases
     • Document icons for config files

7. Emphasize detail
   - Capture each submodule as its own box or collapsed group if too many.
   - Show the plugin registry in core and the Activator mechanism.
   - Don’t overthink—include as many boxes as possible to reflect the modules.

By following these steps, you will produce a comprehensive architecture diagram that maps Weasis’s multi-module Maven build, plugin/OSGi structure, core APIs, functional viewers, and packaging flow, all linked to external DICOM services.
